subject: Clearline Health — Request for SLA concession and commercial repricing
content:
From: Maya Rios <maya.rios@clearlinehealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: billing@clearlinehealth.com, ethan.summers@clearlinehealth.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Severe latency spike week of Nov 2 — request for commercial adjustment

Hi Lauren,

We experienced a sustained latency surge across our patient-search API between Nov 2 02:00–07:30 UTC that materially affected response times for our triage flow. Our engineering team attached a short incident summary and a usage extract so you can see the traffic patterns. This affected two of our key production routes and resulted in a measurable drop in successful flows for several hours.

Given the customer impact and the size of our monthly invoice, we are requesting a commercial adjustment to offset the outage: either a service credit (invoice offset) for November equal to 20% of billed usage or one complimentary month on our reserved capacity plan. We also need an SLA exception documented for the event to help close our internal audit.

Can you advise next steps and what information you need from our side? We’d prefer to resolve this this week.

Thanks,
Maya Rios
Head of Integrations
Clearline Health

Attachments: incident_summary_20261104.pdf (PDF summary), clearline_usage_nov_week1.csv (CSV, 2MB)

---
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Maya Rios <maya.rios@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 13:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency spike week of Nov 2 — request for commercial adjustment

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the quick detail and the attachments. I’ve reviewed the incident summary and the usage export — I agree this was an unacceptable experience and I’m sorry for the impact on Clearline’s triage flows.

I want to move quickly and be transparent about our approach: 1) We’ll escalate for a formal SLO addendum (so the event is documented), 2) we’ll propose a commercial remediation and 3) we’ll ensure our engineering team completes a root-cause writeup within 5 business days.

Commercially, our standard playbook covers credits up to 10% for single-day incidents. Because this spans multiple hours and two critical routes, I’m putting forward an escalated offer that requires exec review: a one-time invoice credit of 20% for the November bill OR a single free month of Reserved capacity (customer choice). Because this exceeds our delegated approval thresholds, I need an exec sign-off to lock it in.

I’m looping in Ben (revenue ops) and Marissa (head of commercial ops) for approval and to coordinate the SLO addendum. Can you confirm which remediation you prefer (credit vs free month) and whether Clearline requires a formal DocuSign for the addendum?

Warmly,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

---
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Clearline Health — request for SLA concession and commercial repricing

Marissa / Vivek —

Forwarding Clearline’s request and the attached incident/usage. TL;DR: They’ve asked for a 20% invoice credit for November or one free month of reserved capacity. Impact is real and the customer is pressing for rapid closure due to an audit.

Key commercial facts:
- Customer: Clearline Health (CL-4782)
- ARR: ~$420k; November billed usage ~ $18.9k
- Estimated token exposure during incident: ~4.6M tokens
- Playbook delegated credit cap for incidents like this: 10% or up to $2,000 (whichever is smaller)

Recommendation: Approve a middle-ground concession to preserve the relationship without setting a high precedent. My suggested settlement: 15% invoice credit applied to November invoice + two weeks of Reserved capacity applied to next billing cycle (equivalent value to ~12% in our margins). Require acceptance of an SLO addendum and a post-incident RCA.

Attachments: incident_summary_20261104.pdf, clearline_usage_nov_week1.csv, proposed_slo_addendum_v2.docx

Please confirm approval or provide edits to the proposed numbers. If we approve, I’ll prepare the DocuSign and notify legal/CS to coordinate the wording.

Thanks,
Lauren

---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clearline Health — request for SLA concession and commercial repricing

Lauren —

I reviewed the incident materials and your recommendation. Approve with a slight modification: offer a 15% invoice credit and two weeks of Reserved capacity is fine, but make the free capacity contingent on Clearline signing the SLO addendum and agreeing to a short-term monitoring plan (30 days) where we provide weekly latency dashboards. Also limit this offer as a one-time commercial remediation and mark the customer file so this does not become a precedent.

Ben — please prepare the invoice adjustment flow and hold issuing the credit until the DocuSign is countersigned. Vivek — FYI for exec awareness; no further escalation needed.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

---
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Maya Rios <maya.rios@clearlinehealth.com>, billing@clearlinehealth.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency spike week of Nov 2 — request for commercial adjustment

Hi Maya —

Thank you for your patience. We reviewed the event and our leadership has approved a one-time remediation. Here’s the settlement we can offer:

- A 15% invoice credit applied to Clearline’s November 2026 invoice (applied as an offset on the next billing cycle).
- Two weeks of Reserved capacity credit applied to your next billing cycle (value roughly aligned to the 15% credit).
- Requirement: Clearline signs the SLO addendum (attached) and we receive the countersigned DocuSign within 10 business days.
- We’ll deliver a full RCA within 5 business days and provide weekly latency dashboards for 30 days as monitoring assurance.

If that works for you, I’ll issue the DocuSign and Ben will prepare the invoice adjustment. If you prefer the single free month option instead of the blended credit + capacity, let me know and I’ll escalate for final approval (that would edge higher than the current concession).

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_slo_addendum_v2.docx (DocuSign-ready)
